Also.description:
A key written alongside a knob. `value` is a literal, with `{value}` standing for the
knob's own rendered value; `bool` and `values` spell the knob's neutral value for this key.

bool.description: The knob's true and false, as this key spells them.

file.description: Another file name; the knob's own by default.

section.description: Another section; the knob's own by default.

value.description: A literal, `{value}` standing for the knob's rendered value.

values.description: The knob's neutral values, as this key spells them.

anyOf.description: Exactly this asset name.
Every `all` substring and none of `none`.

AssetFilter.description: Which release asset: a fixed name, or substrings that must all appear and none that may.

Binding.description:
One knob bound to one key, with the spelling the emulator expects, by the knob's type:
`bool` for `video.fullscreen` and `video.vsync`, `values` for `video.aspect` and `region`,
`scale` for `video.scale`, `text` for `audio.device` (with `values` for `default`) and
`audio.latency_ms` (with a `range`).

also.description:
Keys written alongside every write of this knob (the renderer a scale needs, a second
axis, a mode string beside a flag).

bool.description: `[true, false]` as the emulator spells them (`True`/`False`, `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no`).

note.description: A caveat that makes the knob partial: it is written, and this is what to know.

range.description: `audio.latency_ms`: the milliseconds the emulator takes, lowest and highest.

section.description:
The section (INI), the key path above the key (YAML, XML), or the object under the root
(JSON); empty for the top level.

text.description:
`audio.device` and `audio.latency_ms`: the literal, `{value}` standing for the device's
name or the milliseconds (`"\"{value}\""` where the format quotes). `values` may spell
the device `default` otherwise.

values.description:
Neutral value → the emulator's literal, quotes included where its format wants them.
A neutral value missing here is unsupported, and says so.

anyOf.description:
`flatpak install --user flathub <id>`.
The Flathub app id.
The latest GitHub release of `owner/repo`, one asset of it, extracted into the prefix.

asset.description: Which asset of the latest release.

exe.description: Path of the executable inside the extracted tree.

portable.description: What makes the copy keep its files beside the exe.

anyOf.description: A fixed URL, for projects without GitHub releases. Bumped by catalog PRs.

exe.description: Path of the executable inside the extracted tree.

portable.description: What makes the copy keep its files beside the exe.

sha256.description:
Hex sha256 of the file, bumped with `version` in the same reviewed PR. Validation
rejects a `url` channel without one.

version.description: The version it is, bumped with the URL.

Channel.description: One way to obtain the emulator on one OS.

Config.description:
What `apply` may write into a copy, as the catalog describes it: data, so an emulator with
plain `key = value` settings needs no code at all.

files.description:
Named files under the config root. Knobs, adapters and `Patch::native` refer to them
by name; `main` is the conventional name of the settings file.

knobs.description:
Knob → where it lands, or why it cannot. The knobs are [`KNOBS`]; one not listed here
is reported as not described.

players.description: How player bindings are written. Absent: not described.

ConfigFile.description: One settings file of an emulator.

case_insensitive.description:
INI: the emulator matches section and key names whatever their case (Dolphin), so a
file that spells `[ui]` is edited there rather than given a second `[UI]`.

path.description:
Relative to the config root, for every OS or per OS where the layout differs.
`{config}/` at the start is the settings directory beside a data root: `~/.config/<x>`
for `~/.local/share/<x>`, a Flatpak's `config/<x>` for its `data/<x>`, the root itself
elsewhere.

root.description: XML: the document element the keys hang off (Cemu's `content`).

anyOf.description: Not installable by hermir; the reason, in a phrase a UI shows.

unsupported.description: Why, and what the player does instead.

anyOf.description:
The emulator's own installer: the file goes on its command line, and its exit status is
the verdict.

Code that reads the add-on and puts or registers it where the emulator looks: an adapter
in `content.rs`.

ContentMethod.description: How one kind of add-on is installed.

Detect.description: Detection rules for one OS. Every list is tried; every hit is an `Install`.

flatpak.description: A Flathub app id, looked for in the user and system installations.

paths.description: Absolute paths of the executable, with `~`, `%VAR%` and `$VAR`.

portable_marker.description: A file beside the exe that marks a portable install.

anyOf.description: One path on every OS.
A path per OS.

FilePath.description: A path for every OS, or one per OS.

Firmware.description: Firmware the emulator reads from a folder under its config root, or installs itself.

dir.description:
Relative to the config root: `bios`, `system`, `data`, or `.` for the root itself.
Absent when the emulator only takes firmware through its own installer.

install.description: The emulator's own installer, for firmware that is not loose files.

keys.description:
Firmware the emulator reads from paths its settings name, one key per file, rather than
from a folder (xemu's MCPX boot ROM, flash BIOS and hard-disk image): each file is
copied into `dir` and its key pointed at it, unless the key names a file already there.

platforms.description: Per platform id: what satisfies it.

unpack.description: Firmware that comes as an archive, unpacked into a folder of its own.

FirmwareInstall.description: Firmware the emulator installs from one file (RPCS3's `--installfw <PUP>`).

args.description: The argv after the exe; `{file}` is the firmware file.

done.description:
A file under the config root that exists once firmware is installed. It, not the exit
code, says whether the install worked.

FirmwareKey.description: One firmware file the emulator finds through a key of its settings.

any_of.description:
File name patterns: the first file given that matches, and that no key before this
one took.

ini.description: The ini (or flat TOML) file, under the config root.

note.description: What the file is, in a phrase a UI shows.

optional.description: The emulator also runs without it.

value.description: The value, `{path}` standing for the file's absolute path (`'{path}'` in TOML).

FirmwareNeed.description: What satisfies one platform's firmware need.

any_of.description: File name patterns (`*.bin`, `scph*.bin`); one match is enough.

md5.description:
File name → MD5s of the good dumps of that file, where the name fixes the file
(`dc_boot.bin`). A file of that name with another hash is not placed.

note.description: Where the files come from, in a phrase a UI can show.

optional.description: The emulator also runs without it (an HLE BIOS); its absence is no failure.

FirmwareUnpack.description: An archive of firmware files (a Switch system update as a `.zip` of NCAs), unpacked once.

any_of.description: Archive names (`*.zip`). A match is unpacked, never copied into `dir`.

into.description: Relative to the config root: where the archive's files go.

present.description:
A name pattern that, found in `into`, means firmware is installed. Nothing is unpacked
over it, so firmware the player installed stays.

anyOf.description:
`key` in `[section]` of an ini (or flat TOML) file, set to `value` in place. The file and
section are created when missing; every other line stays as it was. `{root}` in `value`
is the config root's absolute path.

ini.description: The file, under the config root.

value.description: The value, `{root}` standing for the config root's absolute path.

when_unset.description: Only when the key is missing or empty: a value the user chose is kept.

anyOf.description:
A file written only when it does not exist yet: the emulator's own first-run check.
`content` written to `seed` (under the config root) unless it exists.

seed.description: The file, under the config root.

anyOf.description:
A folder under the config root that must exist before the emulator writes into it.
A folder made under the config root.

dir.description: The folder, under the config root.

anyOf.description:
A file the emulator ships beside its exe, copied under the config root once (data an
emulator refuses to start without). Only a copy hermir placed has an exe to copy from.
`copy` (beside the exe) copied to `to` (under the config root) unless it exists.

copy.description: The file, relative to the exe's folder.

to.description: Where it goes, under the config root.

FirstRun.description: One answer to a first-run question, as a file under the config root.

Format.description: How a settings file is patched. Each is a line editor that leaves everything else alone.

oneOf.description:
`key = value` under `[section]`: ini, flat TOML, RetroArch's cfg. An empty section is
the top of the file.
Qt's ini: every key written gets its `key\default=false` companion, or Qt ignores it.
Two-level YAML: `Section:` then `  Key: value`; an empty section is the top level.

Elements by path under the file's `root`; `section` is the path between root and key,
`/`-separated, empty for a child of the root.
A key of the root object, or of the object `section` names directly under it.

anyOf.description: The emulator has no such setting; the note is what a UI shows.

unsupported.description: Why, in a phrase a UI shows.

anyOf.description:
The emulator takes the setting only as a launch flag: `video.fullscreen` through the
launch template's `{fullscreen:…}`. `apply` reports it applied on launch; `launch`
renders it from the request's patch.

note.description: What to know, in a phrase a UI shows.

anyOf.description: Where the knob lands and how it is spelled.

Knob.description: Where a neutral knob lands in an emulator's files, or why it cannot.

Launch.description:
The argv template after the exe. Each argument is a literal or exactly one placeholder:
`{file}` the game, `{fullscreen:<arg>}` `<arg>` when fullscreen is asked for (everything
after the first colon, colons included), `{platform}` the platform id, `{core}` the path of
the libretro core for the platform (RetroArch). Without a game only the `{fullscreen:…}`
arguments are kept, so the emulator opens on its own.

cores.description:
RetroArch: platform id → the libretro core (`snes9x`) `{core}` loads for it, unless the
request names another.

PerOs.description: One slot per OS. A missing key is `None`: honest "not offered here".

PerOs2.description: One slot per OS. A missing key is `None`: honest "not offered here".

PerOs3.description: One slot per OS. A missing key is `None`: honest "not offered here".

PerOs4.description: One slot per OS. A missing key is `None`: honest "not offered here".

PlatformContent.description: One platform's add-ons: how an update and a DLC are installed.

update.description: A game update (a patch the publisher released).

anyOf.description: Not known yet: the note says why, in a phrase a UI shows.
The folders, in the order a UI lists them.

PlatformSaves.description: One platform's saves in the catalog: its folders, or why they are not known.

anyOf.description: A Rust adapter writes them: `crates/hermir/src/config/adapters/<adapter>.rs`.

The emulator picks up SDL pads itself, in the order they appear; there is nothing to
write. The note says so in the emulator's terms.

automatic.description: How the emulator picks pads, in a phrase a UI shows.

anyOf.description: Nothing to write: the note says why.

unsupported.description: Why, in a phrase a UI shows.

PlayersSupport.description: How an emulator's player bindings come to be.

anyOf.description: A file beside the exe.
A folder beside the exe.

Portable.description: What makes the emulator keep its files beside the exe: a marker file or a directory.

ProfileSupport.description:
What a profile is for one emulator: the launch arguments that point it at the profile's
folder, and which of the catalog's files live in there.

args.description: Launch arguments, before the template's; `{profile}` is the profile's folder.

files.description:
Catalog file name → path under the profile's folder. A profile starts as a copy of the
player's own files; a file not named here is patched where it is, snapshotted.

note.description: What else a profile keeps or leaves, in a phrase a UI shows.

native.description: A copy on `PATH` or at a known install path.

portable.description: A copy with its portable marker: `<app>` is its folder.

windows.description: Any copy on Windows, unless it is portable.

SaveDir.description: One folder of saves, as the catalog describes it.

note.description: What to know about the layout inside, in a phrase a UI shows.

path.description:
Relative to the config root; `{data}/` at the start is the data directory beside it
(`~/.local/share/<x>` for `~/.config/<x>`, a Flatpak's `data/<x>` for its `config/<x>`,
the root itself elsewhere); `{game}` alone is beside each game file. Left out when only
`setting` says where (a disk image the player picks).

pattern.description: The files in it that are saves, a glob (`*.ps2`); all of them when left out.

per_game.description: One file or folder per game, rather than one every game shares (a memory card).

setting.description: The setting a player moves the folder with: read first, `path` when it is empty.

units.description:
How the folder splits into units a sync client moves one at a time. Absent: hermir only
says where the folder is.

oneOf.description: The games' own saves: battery RAM, a console's save data, a virtual drive's.
Memory card images the games save to.
Save states: the emulator's snapshots of a running game.

SaveSetting.description: A key of one of the entry's config files that names a save folder.

file.description: The catalog's name for the file.

section.description: The section, `""` for the top level.

then.description: The folder under the one the key names (Cemu's `usr/save` under its `mlc_path`).

unset.description: Values that mean "the default folder", besides an empty one (RetroArch's `default`).

Scale.description: How `video.scale`, a multiplier `n` of the console's resolution, is spelled.

min.description: The smallest multiple the emulator takes.

oneOf.description: `n × 100`, a percentage of the console's resolution (RPCS3).

`n` (as a decimal string, JSON's key) → the emulator's own value; an `n` missing here
is unsupported.
One folder, moved as a tar.

Units.description:
How a save folder splits into units. A unit is named for what it is, so the same save keeps
its name on every machine: a file by its path (`USA/Card A/x.gci` → `USA__Card A__x.gci`),
a folder by its path and `.tar`, or as the folder's adapter names it.

adapter.description:
The adapter that names this folder's units, where a folder is not named for its save
(`ryujinx`, `eden`).

depth.description: Folders only: how many levels below the save folder a unit's folder sits; 1 when unset.

keep.description:
Folders only: globs of the paths inside a unit that are the save; the rest beside it (a
title's DLC in Xenia's content folder) is neither packed nor touched.

shape.description: Each file is a unit, or each folder `depth` levels down.

shared.description: Globs of the files that hold every game's data at once (a shared memory card).

under.description:
Leads every unit name of this folder (`00010004`), so two folders of one shape keep
their units apart.

written_at_start.description:
The emulator writes an empty save the first time a game starts: a unit this machine has
never synced is that empty save, not the player's progress.

Via.description: Where a knob that is not in a file goes.

description: A catalog entry: one emulator, as `catalog/emulators/<id>.json` spells it.

archives.description: It opens a game inside a `.zip` or `.7z` itself.

channels.description: Where to get it, per OS. Empty means detect-and-configure only.

config.description:
How a copy is configured: its settings files, where each neutral knob lands in them,
how its player bindings are written. Absent while nothing is described yet.

content.description: How a game's add-ons reach the emulator, per platform id: its updates and its DLC.

detect.description: How to find a copy the user installed, per OS.

firmware.description:
Where the emulator reads firmware, and what each platform needs there. The folder is
created at install, so a consumer can be granted exactly that one.

first_run.description:
The answers to what a fresh copy asks before it plays anything (a setup wizard, a
welcome box), per OS. `prepare` writes them; each one is what clicking through writes.

id.description: Lowercase, `[a-z0-9-]`, equal to the file name.

launch.description: How to start it with a game.

license.description: SPDX expression of the emulator's own licence.

name.description: The emulator's name, as its project writes it.

no_install.description: Why this entry carries no install channel, when that is deliberate.

notes.description: What to know about it that fits no other field.

profile.description:
How a copy runs on settings of its own, the player's left alone: the emulator's flag
for another config file or folder. Absent where the emulator has none; a profile then
is the in-place, snapshotted patch.

roots.description:
Where the emulator keeps its config and data, per install kind. `<app>` is the exe's
directory, `~` the home, `%VAR%` and `$VAR` environment variables.

saves.description:
Where the player's progress is, per platform id, or `*` for every platform the entry
has: each platform's folders, or why they are not known yet.
